source.title: DAMIR OMERBEGOVIĆ- O BiH nakon izbora o političkom islamizmu - PODCAST ČUŠPAJZ #169

summary.title_hr: DAMIR OMERBEGOVIĆ – O BiH nakon izbora, o političkom islamizmu – PODCAST ČUŠPAJZ #169
summary.abstract_hr: U ovoj epizodi podcasta Čušpajz gost je Damir Omerbegović, društveno-politički komentator rođen u Tuzli koji živi u Pragu. Razgovor počinje izborima u Srbiji, na kojima je studentska lista porazila Vučića, a nastavlja se analizom izbora u Bosni i Hercegovini, odnosa SDA, HDZ-a i SNSD-a te prioriteta nove vlasti poput europskog puta, izmjena izbornog zakona i pitanja OHR-a. Središnji dio posvećen je političkom islamizmu među Bošnjacima, Islamskoj deklaraciji Alije Izetbegovića i stranim utjecajima, pri čemu gost ističe da Bošnjaci kao narod nisu islamisti. U završnom dijelu govori se o migracijama u Europi, češkom pristupu, neredima u Francuskoj, usponu AfD-a i budućnosti Europe, a gost se predstavlja kao optimist.
key_topics: izbori u srbiji i studentski pokret
izbori u bosni i hercegovini i formiranje vlasti
key_points: Gost ocjenjuje da je pobjeda studenata u Srbiji iznenađenje i dobra stvar za regiju jer pokazuje da se autokrata može srušiti demokratskim putem. Uspjeh pripisuje tome što su studenti krenuli od pitanja javne odgovornosti nakon tragedije u Novom Sadu i povezali ljude različitih političkih stavova.
Prema gostu, nova srpska vlast mora krenuti prema demokratizaciji, što uključuje priznavanje povijesnih činjenica i sudskih presuda, ali bez prihvaćanja kolektivne krivnje.

O izborima u BiH gost kaže da treba razlikovati izbornu pobjedu od stvarne političke moći. SDA nije marginalizirana, HDZ je izborom Darijane Filipović u Predsjedništvo ostvario važnu pobjedu, a SNSD je zadržao snagu; Bakira Izetbegovića vidi kao važan faktor u sljedeće četiri godine.

Kao prioritete nove vlasti u BiH gost navodi brži put prema Europskoj uniji, izmjene izbornog zakona i otvoren razgovor o ulozi OHR-a. Smatra da nisu svi problemi posljedica Dejtona, nego i političke kulture u kojoj se kompromis doživljava kao izdaja, te predlaže ponovno razmatranje Travanjskog paketa iz 2006.

Gost od bošnjačke politike očekuje da prihvati institucionalne mehanizme zaštite kolektivnih prava Hrvata i Srba. Smatra da SDA i HDZ mogu ponovno biti partneri jer Izetbegović i Čović imaju prilično tople odnose.

Gost islamizam definira kao političku ideologiju koja određeno tumačenje islama želi pretvoriti u osnovu političkog i društvenog poretka. Naglašava da Bošnjaci kao narod nisu islamisti i da ih je većina sekularizirana, a za otvaranje rasprave o toj temi kaže da nailazi na otpor i islamista i dijela takozvanih progresivnih Bošnjaka.

O migracijama gost tvrdi da je Češka zbog pragmatičnog i strogog pristupa izbjegla probleme kakve imaju Pariz i drugi europski gradovi. Kao početnu pogrešku Europe navodi to što se kritičare migracijske politike odmah žigosalo, a rast AfD-a vidi kao posljedicu toga.
key_topics_en: elections in serbia and the student movement
elections in bosnia and herzegovina and government formation
relations between bosniaks, croats, and serbs
key_points_en: The guest assesses that the victory of the students in Serbia is a surprise and a good thing for the region because it shows that an autocrat can be brought down democratically. He attributes the success to the fact that the students started from the question of public accountability after the tragedy in Novi Sad and connected people of different political views.
According to the guest, the new Serbian government must move toward democratization, which includes acknowledging historical facts and judicial verdicts, but without accepting collective guilt.

Regarding the elections in BiH, the guest says that one must distinguish an electoral victory from actual political power. The SDA is not marginalized, the HDZ achieved an important victory with the election of Darijana Filipović to the Presidency, and the SNSD retained its strength; he sees Bakir Izetbegović as an important factor over the next four years.

As priorities for the new government in BiH, the guest cites a faster path toward the European Union, amendments to the election law, and an open conversation about the role of the OHR. He believes that not all problems are a consequence of Dayton, but also of a political culture in which compromise is perceived as betrayal, and suggests reconsidering the April Package from 2006.

The guest expects Bosniak politics to accept institutional mechanisms for protecting the collective rights of Croats and Serbs. He believes that the SDA and HDZ can be partners again because Izetbegović and Čović have rather warm relations.

The guest defines Islamism as a political ideology that seeks to turn a specific interpretation of Islam into the foundation of the political and social order. He emphasizes that Bosniaks as a people are not Islamists and that the majority of them are secularized, and regarding opening a discussion on this topic, he says it encounters resistance from both Islamists and a portion of the so-called progressive Bosniaks.

Regarding migration, the guest claims that the Czech Republic, due to its pragmatic and strict approach, avoided the problems faced by Paris and other European cities. As Europe's initial mistake, he cites that critics of migration policy were immediately branded, and he sees the growth of the AfD as a consequence of that.
summary.title_en: DAMIR OMERBEGOVIĆ – On BiH after the elections, on political Islamism – PODCAST ČUŠPAJZ #169
summary.abstract_en: In this episode of the Čušpajz podcast, the guest is Damir Omerbegović, a socio-political commentator born in Tuzla who lives in Prague. The conversation begins with the elections in Serbia, in which the student list defeated Vučić, and continues with an analysis of the elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina, relations between the SDA, HDZ, and SNSD, and the priorities of the new government such as the European path, electoral law amendments, and the question of the OHR. The central part is dedicated to political Islamism among Bosniaks, Alija Izetbegović's Islamic Declaration, and foreign influences, with the guest emphasizing that Bosniaks as a people are not Islamists. In the final part, migrations in Europe, the Czech approach, riots in France, the rise of the AfD, and the future of Europe are discussed, and the guest presents himself as an optimist.
